notes: Unused means no row read, written or looked up through the index since the server started (13 min 33 s ago) or since the last ALTER TABLE, CREATE INDEX or DROP INDEX on that table, which restarts its counts. An index used only by a weekly or monthly job looks unused until the job runs.

Tables with no row read or written since the counts started (never opened, or opened only to read their definition) are listed under No data, never as unused. A TRUNCATE of a Performance Schema summary table also resets the counts.
The server has been up only 13 min 33 s, so infrequent jobs may not have run yet.

PRIMARY and UNIQUE indexes are never listed as unused: they enforce constraints even when no query reads them. Indexes that back a foreign key are marked keep: InnoDB checks foreign keys without going through the usage counters.
Foreign keys declared in other schemas that reference mfshop are not checked; a non-unique parent index they use could look unused.
Counts are per server: reads on replicas are not included.

redundant.caveat: Check for FORCE INDEX or USE INDEX hints that name it. Make it invisible first and run a full business cycle (month-end jobs, reports, replicas) before dropping it: an invisible index is still maintained on writes, but the optimizer stops using it, and making it visible again is instant. Queries with an index hint that names it fail while it is invisible.
redundant.why: k_country (country) is a leftmost prefix of k_country_created (country, created_at), so k_country_created serves every lookup k_country serves. Each extra index slows writes and uses buffer pool memory.
